Digital Twins

A living twin of your project supply chain

IntelliByld's Digital Twin is a living, real-time replica of your construction supply chain. It links every material movement to your master schedule, closing the Integration Trap so your digital model mirrors physical site reality.

Physical ↔ digital

One model, continuously reconciled

The site feeds the twin; the twin drives the next decision. Deliveries, weather, and crew status stream into a single live state that schedule, procurement, and carbon all read from.

  • No more reconciliation meetings. The model and the site agree because they share one source of truth.
  • Risks surface early. A drift between plan and reality becomes a flagged threat, not a week-three surprise.
  • Decisions write back. Every re-source or schedule change updates the twin instantly.

What the twin tracks

Four live layers, one picture

Every movement, live

Factory dispatch, GPS in transit, gate arrival - each material's journey is on the map in real time.

Tied to the schedule

Every delivery is linked to the schedule task it unblocks, so a slip shows up as a critical-path risk, not a buried email.

Mirrors the BIM model

The twin speaks IFC. What's modelled, ordered, shipped, and installed stays reconciled in one place.

Carbon as a first-class field

Each movement carries its embodied-carbon weight, so sustainability isn't a separate spreadsheet.

FAQs

Digital Twins, answered

What is the "Integration Trap"?

It's the gap that opens when your BIM model, ERP, and site reality drift apart: the model says one thing, the PO system another, and the foreman a third. The twin closes that gap by linking live material movements directly to the master schedule, so one picture stays true.

How is this different from a BIM model?

A BIM model describes what should be built. The Digital Twin describes what is actually happening to the materials that build it, in real time, and links that back to the schedule. It's the live operational layer on top of the design model.

Where does the live data come from?

Shipment tracking, supplier updates, and site signals flow in through the channels already in use. Pilots start from your BOMs; no rip and replace integration is needed to stand up a working twin.
